# levertags.txt -- PROPOSED `lp:` tags for docs/matching-levers.md.
# Generated by tools/decomp/leverpick_eval.py --propose-tags. Not applied: I cannot write to docs/.
#
# Apply by inserting the comment on the line AFTER the heading, then RE-RUN
# `python3 tools/decomp/leverindex.py` (the regenerating form) because every
# inserted line shifts the heading line numbers the index records. The
# comment itself is invisible to leverindex.build(), which matches only
# `^#{2,3} ` -- verified by `leverpick_eval.py --check-index`.
#
#     ### A `switch` ON A `short` SUBJECT PUTS ...
#     <!-- lp: jumptable s16cast -->
#
# Tags are DERIVED, not judged: a lever's section body names the functions
# it landed, each of those has a fingerprint, and a tag is proposed when
# they agree on a signal more often than its measured prevalence would
# give (share >= 0.67, binomial P(X>=k) <= 0.05, at most 2 tags).
# support is k/n: k of the n attested functions carry it. confidence is
# the binomial tail: high <= 0.001, medium <= 0.01, low <= 0.05.
#
# A LOW-CONFIDENCE ROW ON ONE ATTESTED FUNCTION IS ONE OBSERVATION. It is
# there because the signal is rare enough that one sighting beats chance,
# not because anything corroborated it -- apply those last, or not at all,
# and re-run the eval either way.
#
# FORMAT: one record per lever, tab-separated fields on four lines:
#   lever<TAB>heading text
#   tags<TAB>space-separated
#   support<TAB>tag=k/n ...
#   confidence<TAB>high|medium|low
